The denominator is $4+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $4-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $4-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-10}{4+3\text{i}} & =\frac{-10}{4+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{4-3\text{i}}{4-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-40+30\text{i}}{16-12\text{i}+12\text{i}-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-40+30\text{i}}{16-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-40+30\text{i}}{16-(9)(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-40+30\text{i}}{16+9} \\  & =\frac{-40+30\text{i}}{25}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-40+30\text{i}}{25}=-\frac{40}{25}+\frac{30}{25}\text{i}=-\frac{8}{5}+\frac{6}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
